summary: Use bitwise operators (XOR, AND, OR, shifts) to exploit binary structure for O(1) per-element tricks, avoiding extra space that a hash set or sort would require.
recognize_when: The problem involves finding a single/odd-occurring element among duplicates (XOR cancels pairs)
You need to count set bits, check powers of two, or manipulate individual bits of a number
Constraints ask for O(1) extra space where a hash-based solution would use O(n)
The problem mentions binary representation directly, or subsets/masks over a small fixed number of elements
You need to swap, toggle, isolate, or clear specific bits without arithmetic overflow concerns

complexity.notes: Each element or bit is processed in a single pass with constant-time bitwise operations; no auxiliary data structure is needed.

gotchas: Assuming XOR-based tricks work when there are more than one unpaired element (need extra partitioning logic)
Forgetting Python ints are arbitrary precision, so masking with & 0xFFFFFFFF is needed to simulate fixed-width overflow
Confusing bitwise operators (&, |, ^) with logical ones (and, or) or misusing signed right shift on negative numbers
